behavior: Existing Unlock remains accessible for unresolved operations when command preparation is not active; it opens a dedicated recovery dialog without changing Home layout or adding Home command cards/notifications.
Dialog entry and Check status perform read-only reconciliation. Opening, refreshing, dismissing or relaunching never retries a command automatically.

Only the explicit Retry the same request action invokes existing retrySameRequest, which queries again and may resend only the original requestId/deviceId/doorId. Current preferred target is never consulted by recovery.
Known pending, sent and unknown receipts offer reconciliation only. Terminal and error messages use localized existing command wording; acknowledgement is not presented as physical passage.
Provider's existing persistence, request/target checks, concurrent-command lock and generation/ownership guards remain unchanged.
Dialog captures session epoch/token on creation, hides old status and disables recovery on session change; even a new session for the same employee requires closing and reopening the dialog.

Failed request lookup or failed local restore leaves the protected intent intact and provides further status-check/retry access as applicable. Permission denial from a retry is shown without clearing uncertainty.

correctedBehaviorScenarios: First command TimeoutError, request lookup null, Home refresh and provider recreation preserve the original intent while keeping recovery accessible.
Dialog entry queries before retry; explicit double tap creates only one retry using identical request ID and original target despite a different preferred door.
In-flight retry blocks another target; terminal confirmation clears persistence without inferring physical passage or displaying a Home status card.
Failed lookup remains recoverable and an explicit retry whose lookup also fails sends no mutation.
Retry transitions to pending, hides resend, and terminal failure is reconciled without another command.
Logout during lookup prevents resend and preserves scoped persistence; new same-employee session cannot reactivate stale dialog but can reopen recovery.
Revoked permission is displayed while original uncertainty continues to block another target.
Failed local-store restore exposes read-only checking, then exposes same-request retry only after restoring the original intent.
An existing pending receipt found during explicit retry is accepted without resubmission.
TR and EN dialog controls expose semantics and remain usable at 320 logical-pixel width and 2x text.
